message.content:
In most eukaryotic cells, the number of mitochondria varies widely depending on the cell’s metabolic demands and developmental stage. Typical ranges include:

| Cell Type / Context | Approximate Mitochondrial Count |
|---------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Typical somatic cell** (e.g., fibroblast) | ~200–500 per cell |
| **Highly active cells** (muscle fibers, neurons) | Thousands to tens of thousands |
| **Stem cells** (low energy demand) | ~50–100 per cell |
| **Cancer cells** (often high metabolism) | Can exceed 1,000 per cell |

These figures are averages; individual counts can fluctuate due to factors such as cell cycle phase, differentiation status, and environmental conditions.
